newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals give back gains to end lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals give back gains to end lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly lower Wednesday, with the exception of silver, after the complex firmed early in the session on the back of a sharp rise in U.S. first quarter GDP.
"Direction is a bit unclear right now," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
"Gold and silver have been drifting lower recently, but keeps running into support around $340 or $339.50 and looking like it wants to rally, before it fails again," he said.
COMEX June gold ended down 40 cents at $341.20, after slipping back from early session highs at $343.20.
In the bullion market spot gold ended quoted $339.30/80, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $340.15 and the New York close Tuesday around $339.70/20.
Early in the session gold and silver gained on news U.S. of surge in U.S. economic growth in the first quarter which revived inflationary fears.
U.S. first quarter GDP rose rose 5.6 percent, against expectations for a 4.1 percent rise, while the implicit price deflator rose 2.3 percent versus expectations for a 1.7 percent rise.

Gold prices found some support Tuesday also, after better than expected U.S. data on wage inflation helped U.S. treasury bonds rally sharply, taking some of the pressure off precious metals which are not interest bearing assets.
But daily momentum oscillators for COMEX June gold remain in negative territory, analysts said, after a new contract low was seen last week at $339.50.

Meanwhile, some analysts and bullion bankers believe fresh undisclosed European central bank activity has been an ongoing reality, and not just a threat, in the past two months, and is responsible for the renewed slide in gold prices in the past two months.

The slide in gold prices from around $360 an ounce in early March occurred without much commodity fund participation as funds were relatively inactive until the past two weeks, according to the CFTC data, analysts noted.

Some gold miners have also increased their hedging activity in recent months as prices have weakened, partly in the belief that central bank selling may drive gold prices lower still, one analyst said.
For example, Australian gold producer, Sons of Gwalia Ltd said on April 18 it had increased its hedge position to 5.054 million ounces from 3.1 million ounces.
The spot gold/silver ratio has been little changed in this week, ending Wednesday at 72.5 down from 73.0 Tuesday.
But COMEX July silver ended up 2.3 cents at $4.693 an ounce, after recovering to $4.760 intraday.
In London Tuesday, spot silver fixed at $4.6425, its lowest in two years, following the slide COMEX July silver to a new contract low at $4.630 on Monday.
NYMEX July platinum ended down $3.00 at $370.60, while NYMEX June palladium lost $1.30 to $156.20.
Lending in the platinum group metal physical market allowed implied lease rates for platinum and palladium to ease Wednesday and this was reflected in futures market prices, analysts said.
